one_month_reasoning: Q3 2026 results fall inside the window. Rambus has not announced the date, but its last four reports came on Mondays, so the most likely date is Oct 26-27 and the chance it lands before 2026-11-01 is about 95%. The guide is revenue $210-216M, product $110-116M, royalties $69-75M (lumpy after an elevated Q2) and EPS $0.75-0.82. Rambus has beaten guidance in recent quarters, so a beat is likely. Against that, all four of the last prints fell the next day: -8.7% (Oct-25), -13.4% (Feb-26), -21.3% (Apr-26; I had wrongly said -11% in round 1) and -9.0% (Jul-26). The stock has also run +39% from its $80.39 close on Sep-14, and the $100M ASR dealer bid has most likely ended (the 8-K says it completes by the end of Q3). One more caution: Montage, the main RCD competitor, grew Q2 revenue +28% q/q, which sets a high bar for Rambus's product guide to show it is keeping pace. I put the median at about $110, slightly below spot, with a monthly sigma of about 19%. That is roughly the 80%/3.5 rule, trimmed because the realized vol includes the spring spike, with a little extra weight on the downside gap. P(close >= $111.97) is 0.46. I do not go further, because four prints is a small sample and a beat combined with strong product and companion-chip guidance could extend the memory momentum trade.

fair_value.method: A 70/30 blend of forward P/E (NTM EPS at Oct-2027 of $4.00 x 28 = $112, with no separate net-cash add because EPS already includes interest income) and FCF yield (NTM FCF $370M less ~$50M share-settlement taxes = $320M at a 3.0% EV yield = $10.67B, plus ~$0.76B net cash, over 109M shares = $105). Blended value is about $110.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM non-GAAP EPS at Oct-2027 $4.00 (0.25 x FY27 $3.58 + 0.75 x FY28 $4.15) x 28x; no net-cash add

inputs_detail.derivation: Q1 $0.63 + Q2 $0.77 (reported) + Q3 guide midpoint $0.785 + Q4 ~$0.84. This matches the $3.04 consensus on stockanalysis.

The $3.72 consensus cannot be verified (the page is paywalled), so I treat it as an upper anchor. Bottom-up: FY26 $3.03 grown ~18%, from RDIMM unit growth slowing to 12-15% (Baird) plus companion-chip and MRDIMM content gains. Montage's +26.7% H1 growth shows the category is still expanding fast.
FY27 grown ~16%, with MRDIMM becoming material on AMD Venice and Diamond Rapids (slipped to 2027) and the shift to smaller 32/64GB modules lifting module counts per bit.

Spot is ~37x FY26 and ~31x FY27. I expect the multiple to compress toward high-20s as growth settles in the mid/high teens. Montage, a direct peer, trades at a premium on faster growth, which argues against going lower. Net cash is not added because interest income (~$28M/yr) is already in EPS.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: NTM FCF at horizon $370M less ~$50M share-settlement taxes = $320M / 3.0% = $10.67B EV + $0.76B net cash, over 109M shares

inputs_detail.derivation: Per the 10-Q, OCF is after a $30.7M inventory build, and capex was $20.7M.
H1 FCF of $123.8M annualized is ~$248M; adding back part of the one-off $30.7M inventory build gives ~$270-290M.
$280M compounded ~17% a year for ~1.75 years, in line with my EPS path.
H1 2026 net-share-settlement taxes were $52.7M, which is front-loaded by vesting seasonality. I deduct about half of a ~$100M annual rate as a real recurring cash cost of stock compensation.
This corresponds to ~33x EV/FCF after the stock-comp tax deduction, consistent with a high-20s P/E on unadjusted EPS.
$824.9M at 6/30/26, less the $100M ASR prepay (8-K 2026-08-05), plus ~$40M of net Q3 cash generation. No debt.
110M guided diluted shares, less ~1M retired by the $100M ASR at ~$95.

bear.story: RDIMM unit growth slows below Baird's 12-15% because DRAM wafers go to HBM. Montage keeps out-shipping Rambus on newer RCD generations and MRDIMM, and royalties stay lumpy. The DOJ antitrust probe adds overhang and the memory momentum trade unwinds. The stock goes to ~22x on ~$3.3 NTM EPS. I made this less likely than in round 1 because TrendForce's 15-20% is bit supply and smaller modules mean units can grow faster than bits.

base.story: RCD share holds near 40%, PMIC and companion chips grow, and MRDIMM becomes material in 2027 on Venice, then Diamond Rapids. NTM EPS at the horizon is ~$4.00 and the multiple settles at ~28-29x.

bull.story: The AI-server cycle broadens to general compute, MRDIMM ramps on both platforms, and companion-chip share reaches 40-50%. EPS beats by 10-15% (NTM ~$4.5) and memory names keep a ~40x momentum multiple.

thesis_break_reason: $71 is about 9% below the $77.89 March low and about 18x NTM EPS of ~$4.00. The stock did not trade there even after the April -21% print or the summer DOJ/sector selloff. Getting there would most likely need a guided sequential decline in product revenue (RDIMM units contracting or RCD share loss to Montage), a shortfall in a royalty renewal with a top licensee (the top two customers are ~38-40% of revenue), or a DOJ indictment that forces changes to licensing practices.

Competitive pace against Montage, whose Q2 revenue rose +28% q/q and whose 3rd/4th-generation RCDs exceed 50% of its RCD output

Multiple compression from ~31x FY27 as growth normalizes, and the memory momentum trade unwinding
The DOJ criminal antitrust grand-jury subpoena (a risk factor since Q1 2026), an undatable left tail
reasoning: I took the supervisor's verified corrections. The Q1 reaction was -21.3%, not -11%, and all four of the last prints fell. My P/E leg double-counted net cash: I added $7.5/share on top of EPS that already includes interest income, and I used $825M without netting the $100M ASR. My FCF base used Q2 OCF alone when H1 FCF was $123.8M. The $3.72 FY27 consensus is unverified. Fixing these lowers fair value from $116 to $110. The P/E leg falls to $112 because the cash add is removed and FY27 is re-based bottom-up to $3.58, which still gives NTM $4.00 on a correct 1/4 FY27 + 3/4 FY28 weighting. The FCF leg stays near $105: a higher base (~$280M) is offset by deducting the share-settlement taxes the supervisor flagged. I also accept the supervisor's bits-versus-units point and cut the bear probability from 0.25 to 0.22. Following the source review, I dropped the StocksToTrade/Timothy Sykes newsletters and the Simply Wall St forum narrative as evidence, and looked for independent alternative signals instead. (1) Hiring: Revelio Labs shows 96 active postings in 2026, down 27% from 116 in 2025, with new postings at ~30 a month versus 54 in 2023, and headcount ~822 (+1.5% y/y). That reads as opex discipline that supports margins, not a growth push, and is neutral to slightly positive for EPS. TrueUp and Migrate Mate show varying counts (59 and 16), so the level is noisy, but the direction is the same. (2) Channel/competitor check: Montage's H1 2026 revenue was RMB 3.335B (+26.7% y/y) and Q2 was +28.3% q/q, a record. Montage says its 3rd/4th-generation DDR5 RCDs exceed 50% of its RCD output and its 2nd-generation MRCD is in trial use. Rambus product revenue grew +22% y/y in Q2, comparable on a y/y basis, so share loss is not shown and I agree with the supervisor. But Montage's sequential momentum is stronger, so I keep a competitive risk in the bear case. One search snippet claimed RMB 5.1B and +53% for Montage interconnect; the fetched article does not support it and I ignore it. (3) Pricing tracker: RAM Prices USA's Amazon index shows DDR5 retail at ~$18/GB at end-September 2026, roughly double late-2025. Together with TrendForce's +13-18% q/q server contract prices, this confirms tight supply and healthy module demand, but Rambus has no direct pricing leverage. I could not reach X/Twitter, Reddit or Substack content on RMBS through search, so I have no reliable social signal. Distribution: lognormal with median ~$113 and sigma 0.55, mixed 80/20 with a sigma-0.70 component for the 80% realized vol and earnings-gap and DOJ tails. The lower strikes are slightly raised to match the reduced bear probability. The resulting P(>=112) is about 0.51. Total queries this round: 7.
